_note: What MyThuso can actually do, and what it only draws. Every screen used to carry its own hand-typed 'Design preview', 'Demonstration record' or 'Fictional workspace' — sixty-odd sentences saying roughly the same thing in slightly different words, some of them on screens whose function was by then real, and none of them connected to anything that would know. This file is the one place that knows. A capability is connected or it is not; a screen asks, and the notice is rendered from here or not rendered at all. When an integration lands, one boolean changes and the sentence disappears from every platform at once.
_honestyNote: Turning `connected` to true is a claim about the world, not about the code, so scripts/check-boundaries.mjs refuses it unless `evidence` names a file that exists and the capability's `blockedBy` list is empty. A health service that overstates its readiness is not a marketing problem, and the way that happens is never a lie — it is somebody tidying a banner off a layout at eleven at night.

capabilities.name: Accounts and sign-in
blockedBy: An SMS provider for one-time codes.
DNS and TLS on mythuso.co.za, because a one-time-code endpoint over plain http hands out accounts.
capabilities.notice: Sign-in is not switched on yet. This account is local to your browser and disappears when you close it.

capabilities.name: Booking a visit
blockedBy: A nurse roster with real availability.
Payment, because a visit nobody can pay for is not booked.
capabilities.notice: This does not book a visit. Nobody is dispatched and nothing is charged.

capabilities.name: Taking payment
blockedBy: A South African payment provider, contracted and integrated.
A merchant account.
capabilities.notice: No payment is taken. The prices shown are the catalogue's and no card is charged.

capabilities.name: Paying a nurse
blockedBy: A payment provider.
Verified bank details, which need the identity service switched on.
capabilities.notice: No money moves. These figures are the catalogue's arithmetic on sample visits.

capabilities.name: Confirming a credential with the body that issued it
blockedBy: An agreement or accreditation with each of the thirteen authorities. All thirteen adapters answer not-integrated.
A contracted identity provider for the identity check.
capabilities.notice: No credential on this screen has been confirmed with the body that issued it. A reviewer has looked at a document the applicant supplied, which is not the same thing.

capabilities.name: Dispatching a nurse
blockedBy: Live positions from nurse devices.
An accepted-visit protocol.
Booking, which is what would create something to dispatch.
capabilities.notice: Dispatch is not connected. These positions and visits are sample data, drawn from real coordinates.

capabilities.name: Holding a clinical record
blockedBy: The controls in docs/PRIVACY-AND-SECURITY.md.
An Information Officer's sign-off on retention.
SA-resident hosting for special personal information.
capabilities.notice: This record is sample data. Nothing you type here is stored, and no real record exists behind this screen.

capabilities.name: The consultation call
blockedBy: No media stack. Neither app declares a camera or microphone permission, deliberately.
A doctor panel with a real rota.
capabilities.notice: This build has never asked this device for the camera or the microphone, and no connection is opened. What follows is the design of a consultation, drawn at full size.

capabilities.name: AI-assisted screening
blockedBy: No model, no vendor and no licence. The frame around it — provenance, sign-off, conflict resolution — is built; the screening is not.
capabilities.notice: Nothing here is screened by software. The frame around a result is real; the result is sample data.

capabilities.name: Talking to MyThuso
blockedBy: No speech model, no vendor and no licence — the same gap as screening, and the same procurement decision.
No microphone permission is declared on either native app, deliberately. Declaring one is not a build step; it is a decision about recording people in their homes.
Nothing has been designed for what happens to a recording of a person describing a symptom. Until that is answered under POPIA, there is nothing to switch on.
capabilities.notice: MyThuso cannot listen to you. Nothing here has a microphone, no speech is recorded or sent anywhere, and this is a drawing of an assistant rather than one.
capabilities.neverSoften: No microphone affordance may be drawn — not an enabled one, not a disabled one, not a decorative one. A control that looks like it is listening and is not is worse than no control, and on a health product it is the kind of worse that gets believed.

capabilities.name: The connected kit
blockedBy: No device is contacted. No Bluetooth or eSIM permission is declared.
capabilities.notice: No device is connected. These readings are sample data and no instrument has been paired.

capabilities.name: Sending a prescription to a pharmacy
blockedBy: A contracted pharmacy network.
A pharmacist's review of the substitution classes.
capabilities.notice: No prescription reaches a pharmacy. The substitution rules on this screen are real and have not been read by a pharmacist.

capabilities.name: Booking an interpreter
blockedBy: No interpreter is contacted.
SATI's accreditation route for SASL is drafted and unconfirmed.
capabilities.notice: No interpreter is contacted. The roster and the refusals are real; the people on it are not.

capabilities.name: Reaching a person
blockedBy: No SMS, email or push provider.
capabilities.notice: Nothing is sent. No message, invitation or reminder reaches anybody.

capabilities.name: The emergency pathway
blockedBy: No contracted ambulance partner.
No urgent rota.
The routing questions have not been reviewed by a clinician.
capabilities.notice: This does not call anybody. In a real emergency dial 10177 or 112 from your phone.
capabilities.neverSoften: The ambulance number on this screen is real and always shown first, connected or not. The one refusal on this pathway that is not about MyThuso is the one that matters most.

rules.statement: A screen renders the notice for the capability it depends on. Not three of them stacked, and not one it does not use.
rules.why: A nurse's schedule carried a Design preview banner, a WORKSPACE · DEMO eyebrow and a Fictional workspace paragraph before any content — three sentences saying one thing, filling the screen above the first visit. A reader who is told the same thing three times has been told it none.

rules.statement: No screen writes its own not-connected sentence. It names a capability and the sentence is rendered from this file.
rules.why: Sixty hand-typed variations cannot be switched off together, and some of them will be wrong. One place that knows means one boolean to change when an integration lands.

rules.statement: A capability may be marked connected only when `evidence` names a file that exists and `blockedBy` is empty. The build refuses it otherwise.
rules.why: The failure mode is never a lie. It is somebody clearing a banner off a layout because the screenshot looked better without it.

rules.statement: A role switcher, a state picker and a gallery of loading states are development tools. They are removed from what ships, and removing them says nothing about whether anything is connected.
rules.why: The two got tangled: taking the demo furniture out felt like claiming the product was live. They are separate questions and this file answers only the second.

_permissionsNote: Neither app declares a single permission — no uses-permission in the Android manifest, no NS*UsageDescription on the iOS target. That is the strongest true sentence this product can say about itself, and several notices above depend on it: "nothing here has a microphone" is a special case of "nothing here asks for anything". A permission may be added only when a capability here names it under requiresPermissions, which forces whoever wants it to say which feature it serves, beside what is blocking that feature. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs fails an undeclared one on either platform — a whitelist, because the earlier version named RECORD_AUDIO and the microphone key specifically and would have let CAMERA or a location key through unnoticed.
